references.text: The same instruction regarding carrying poles of acacia wood overlaid with gold is given for the ark. This shows the consistent pattern for how holy objects were to be carried in the tabernacle.
Carrying poles of acacia wood are also used for the bronze altar, but these are overlaid with bronze instead of gold, showing a difference in degrees of holiness.
The incense altar also has carrying poles of acacia wood overlaid with gold, following the same pattern as the table of showbread.
Fulfillment of the instruction regarding the carrying poles for the table of showbread, where Bezalel makes them from acacia wood and overlays them with gold.
Describes how the table of showbread was to be covered and carried by the Levites during the wilderness journey, where the carrying poles were necessary for transport.
At the dedication of Solomon's temple, the carrying poles on the ark are mentioned, showing that this tradition of carrying poles continued in the holy objects of the temple.
Complementary parts of the same instruction regarding the table's carrying poles.
Fulfillment of the command: From instruction (Exod 25:28) to execution (Exod 37:15).
Theological contrast between the gold overlay of the table and the bronze overlay of the altar.
The principle of gold overlay on carrying poles is repeated for the incense altar.
Narrative parallel: The execution of the incense altar's poles mirrors that of the table.
Confirmation of the repeated material principle for holy carrying poles.
Contrast: Bronze for the altar of burnt offering versus gold for the table.
Practical application: Use of the carrying poles for the golden altar during the wilderness journey.
